_comment: Teaching/lore NPC on the actor model (plan-entity-model.md chunk 3a) — formerly a statless model/npc type placed from zone.npcs, now an ordinary actor carrying an interaction block. role creature + speed 0 (PO 2026-07-27, D4): an NPC is an actor that authors no movement, not a kind of its own. Unattackable by two AUTHORED knobs (D5): faction townsfolk (friendlyToPlayers ⇒ player damage skips it) and collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) — solid and streamed, but deliberately NOT on Action(2), so no aura on either side can target it. interaction.range 2.0 [PLACEHOLDER] is the talk reach and, being the wider of the two (D7), sizes the one sensor — which is also the audience interaction.ambient fans out to. The pre-merge aggroRadius 1.0 stayed as authored but no longer governs anything: under D21 leaving talk range now ENDS a conversation, and 1.0 leaves less standing room than the two bodies take up (L26). experience 0 keeps it off the nameplate path; the health bar is accepted (D3). All values [PLACEHOLDER]. Teaches Pickaxe, which is the only thing that clears a Rockfall (the gated 'smash' tag). ⚑ QUESTS (plan-quests.md C4): the MIDDLE of `the-lost-lamp`, and the only NON-TERMINAL advance_quest edge in the first pass — his row moves ask_miner → clear_den and ends nothing, which is exactly what C1's derived terminality and C2's two-phase cross-validation exist to get right. It carries no reward, and under L10 it may not: grant_xp is legal only on an edge that ends a quest, because abandon leaves the lifetime counters standing.
name: Miner

lines: The one sitting in the dark sent you, did he. He's been sitting there three days.

grants.line: North of the tunnel, where the trees thin out and the ground turns to scree. Half a dozen of them at least — and nobody has ever got anything back off a kobold by asking.

lines: We need the Militia to clear this tunnel once and for all... They are so useless

grants.line: The tunnel is overrun! Take my Pickaxe, I have no use for it anymore.
